subject: Your property tax bill is probably wrong — here's the 30-min fix
preheader: 30-40% of rental properties over-assessed · $400-1,800/yr saved per property · 62% appeal success rate

marketSnapshot.headline: Property tax appeals — the under-used profit lever
marketSnapshot.body: Counties over-assess about 30-40% of rental properties relative to actual sale-comp values. Most investors glance at the assessment notice, file it, and move on — that's a mistake. The appeal process exists specifically to correct over-assessments and the average successful appeal saves $400-1,800 per year, in perpetuity. On a 5-property portfolio, that's $2,000-9,000/yr of free NOI for ~30 minutes per property of paperwork.

dealSpotter.address: Example: tax bill $4,200 · comp-supported value 12% lower
dealSpotter.body: $285k purchase. Current assessed value $268k = $4,200 tax bill. Recent sales of comparable properties in the area: $245-262k. Filing a formal appeal with three recent comps has a 65-75% success rate in most counties. If granted, the tax bill drops to ~$2,950, which adds $1,250/yr to NOI. Cap rate moves from 7.4% to 7.8% on that single piece of paperwork.

dealSpotter.address: Example: assessment matches comps · skip the appeal
dealSpotter.headlineNumber: Tax $1,950 — assessed fairly · don't risk reassessment
dealSpotter.body: Don't appeal a fair assessment — the county can reassess upward and you'll cost yourself money. Only appeal when comps clearly support a LOWER value. Default to 'assess your assessment' before deciding.

dealSpotter.headlineNumber: Appeal saves $650/yr · 70%+ success rate when armed with comps
dealSpotter.body: Some counties (Davidson TN, parts of NY, parts of CA) require a formal hearing rather than paper-only appeal. Slightly more work — 10-15 min hearing typically by phone or video. The success rate when you show up with three solid comparable sales is high. Most investors don't bother. The ones who do compound this advantage over years of ownership.

blogFeature.title: How to spot a bad rental deal in 60 seconds — 7 red flags
blogFeature.excerpt: Property tax-to-value ratio is one of the seven red flags. The flag isn't 'high tax' — it's 'tax relative to actual market value is out of line, signaling either an over-assessment or a hidden problem with the property.'

qa.question: Step by step: how do I actually appeal a property tax assessment?
qa.answer: Three steps that work in 90% of counties. (1) Pull 3-5 sales comparables of similar properties (same bedroom count, similar age, within 1 mile, sold in the last 12 months). Most county assessor sites have a comparable-sales lookup tool; if not, your realtor can pull this in 5 minutes. (2) Calculate the median price per square foot from those comps. Multiply by your property's square footage to get a comp-supported value. (3) File the appeal through your county's online portal (look for 'tax assessment appeal' on the assessor's site). Attach the comp list and your calculation. Most counties charge $25-100 to file. Hearings are usually in writing; some require a 10-minute call. Decisions come back in 60-120 days. If you win, the savings start immediately and recur every year you own the property. Set a calendar reminder for next year's assessment notice — the savings only persist if you defend them again when assessments roll forward.
